segments.text: Welcome to the video demonstration of the database systems coursework from group number 3.
In deliverable 1.1, we normalize the customer city product and order item tables to 3 and F.
Originally, the primary key of the customer city table was ID.
But while unleashing the order item table, there was no relationship defined.
But we found that ID in customer city and the customer city ID in the order item table matched.
So the column was renamed to customer city ID to clearly establish the relationship.
In the customer city table, the transitive dependency existed between the county, region, country and the city.
So this was resolved by splitting the table into customer 3 and F on city 3 and F.
With the city ID acting as a surrogate key and later it was referenced by the foreign key between the customer 3 and F on city 3 and F.
In the product table, the composite key caused partial dependencies.
So the table was split into product group, variant group, product 3 and F on variant 3 and F.
Here the important design aspect is product group was not dependent on variant code as it violates the 2NF.
So it must be split into its own table.
So a product group was split into the one table.
To link this table, variant group table was created, which I had a one, many to many relationship between these two tables.
Next order item table was normalized.
In the order item table, the table was already in 2NF.
In 3NF, the line item total was acting as a derived attribute as it can be calculated by using quantity and the unit price.
So this column was removed from the table so it can be computed later.
So next moving into the create order item stored procedure.
Here the validation checks for order number must be already present in the database.
Order item number must be unique and product code, variant code and the unit price combination must already exist.
So if I just try to give quantity, invalid number, when I try to run this, it should be getting failed because the quantity must be greater than 0.
So this is one of the invalid quantity number.
So giving a positive quantity number should make this transaction successful.
So running this, the transaction is successful.
So these are the validation checks we have taken.
And if I try to run this again, the transaction will be rolled back.
So because order number, item number already exist for this order.
So this wraps the delivery one.
We will now briefly explain D2 which is our BI solution developed using SQL server analysis services.
We started by restoring the final database backup produced in D1 which contains the fully normalized tables and validated transactional data.
After restoring the database, we created a data source view which links the tables as for the referencing of foreign keys.
We then created several dimensions to support business analysis.
Tables containing descriptive attributes were modeled as dimensions while transactional tables containing measurable business values were modeled as fact tables.
For example, the date dimension was designed with a natural hierarchy where a day rolls into month, month rolls into quarter and quarter rolls into the year.

The fact order table represents transactional order data at the product variant level and contains measurable values such as quantity and sales amount along with foreign keys linking to the relevant dimensions.
Using this fact table, we built the queue following a star schema design which supports consistent aggregation and helps avoid double counting.
Overall, deliverable two presence are fully validated proof of concept, BI solution that meets all the assignment requirements and accurately reflects the underlying data.
